subject: Sandbox prompts & output storage — confirmation and next steps
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Julia Nguyen <julia.ng@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Sandbox prompts & output storage — confirmation and next steps

Hi Julia,

Great to meet you and the Novus team on the call earlier — thanks for sharing the demo flow and the examples of sandbox prompts. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the commitments we discussed around prompt/output handling in the Redwood sandbox and lay out the suggested next steps. Please see the summary below and call out anything I missed.

Quick recap of your asks from the call:
- Confirm what parts of the prompt and assistant output are persisted in Redwood sandbox by default (full payload, redaction options).
- Clarify default retention windows (TTL) for prompt/input payloads, outputs, and diagnostic logs.
- Confirm logging and access controls (who at Redwood and your org can access data).
- Options for data residency (US-only) for sandbox/testing and path to private/VPC deployment.

Redwood sandbox (default behavior we discussed):
- Prompts & outputs: retained by default for 30 days in encrypted object storage; retained to support debugging, quality monitoring, and evals.
- Diagnostic logs (routing, latency, and model selection): retained for 90 days by default. Logs contain request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts) but do not store unredacted customer-side secrets by policy (we encourage emptying sensitive fields before sending).
- KV cache / in-memory state: ephemeral only — not persisted to disk in sandbox.
- Access controls: Redwood SRE and support have role-based access; accesses are audited. We provide an export on request and can configure narrower access for enterprise customers.
- Residency: Hosted sandbox is US-region by default. For US-only requirements we can pin sandbox traffic to US-hosted clusters; for regulated production, Private deployment (VPC) is recommended.

Proposed next steps (from Redwood):
1) Security one-pager (attached) with field-level breakdown and retention/TTL options.
2) Short tech call with our security engineer to run through your MPP (minimum product plan) examples where PII appears in prompts (Marissa is cc'd).
3) If you want US-only sandbox pinning, we can enable that for your org and provide a short runbook.
4) Draft a short mutual action plan with specific TTLs/SLAs for the PoC and production.

Attachments included: redwood-sandbox-data-handling-one-pager.pdf (summary), novus-mpp-questions.xlsx (your example prompts we took notes on).

Would you be able to confirm the scope you want Redwood to preserve (full prompt vs. redacted) and preferred TTL for the PoC by end of day Monday? I’ll schedule the Marissa technical sync for Tuesday based on your availability.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ava — helpful summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock in TTLs:

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Nguyen <julia.ng@novushealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 16:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Sandbox prompts & output storage — confirmation and next steps

Hi Julia — thanks for the questions. Quick answers below (keeping to what applies to the hosted sandbox). Happy to expand on any item on the tech call.

1) Retention semantics:
- Prompts/inputs & outputs: TTL is measured from ingestion (first write). For the hosted sandbox default this is 30 days from the timestamp the request enters our system. There is no automatic "last-access" extension in sandbox mode.
- Diagnostic logs: 90 days from ingestion.

2) Field-level redaction and PII detection:
- We offer an optional pre-ingestion pipeline (PII detector) as a configurable add-on that can identify common PHI types (SSN, MRN, DOB, email, phone) and either mask or drop those fields before data is written to storage. 
- For the PoC we can enable a lightweight detector in sandbox to automatically mask high-confidence SSN/MRN patterns; this runs inline before persistence. Detection is configurable and produces an audit trail of masked fields (audit entries do not include original values).

3) Synthetic PHI in sandbox:
- Treated identically to other payloads for retention and logging.
- We recommend tagging test traffic via a request header (x-redwood-test: true) so we can apply different logging/monitoring rules or exclude it from production analytics if desired.

4) KV cache & token storage:
- KV cache used for autoregressive decoding is in-memory on the serving node and is not persisted to object storage in sandbox. It is evicted per model session and none of the per-request KV cache is written to disk.
- Token-level accounting (counts for billing/trace) is captured in aggregated telemetry records (token counts, model id) but not stored with unredacted prompt text in long-term logs by default. Full request payloads are the object storage items that get the 30-day TTL; the aggregated telemetry is retained separately for 90 days for analytics.

5) Access and audit:
- Access to stored prompt/output objects is role-based; support/SE/SRE accesses are recorded in our audit log. We can provide periodic access reports and a custom export for your SOC review.

If Novus wants US-only sandbox pinning, we can do that and we will reflect the pinning in the one-pager and runbook. On the Tue call we can scope whether you want the PII detector enabled and whether masked values suffice for your PoC.

Attachments: I attached a short appendix to the one-pager that lists the default fields we detect and masking behavior.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Security & Privacy Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
